gap: No result ChatGPT got states that techtest.org measured 277.6 Wh out of 288 Wh (96%) from the Anker SOLIX C300X DC's 12 V socket at 2 A (about 24 W, a router-plus-modem-sized load) and 271.5 Wh (94%) on USB-C at 9 V/3 A (about 27 W). It also does not state that The Solar Lab measured the inverter-free EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC using about 2 Wh in 24 hours switched on with no load, while Gough Lui measured 1.14 W idle on the EcoFlow RIVER 2 and The Technology Man saw a BLUETTI EB3A lose 16% in 12 hours with DC on and nothing plugged in.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rivals. Best Batteries (en/us '46 measurements') gives only the C300X DC average of 272.9 Wh, with no breakdown by port or load. ChatGPT itself said it would 'want a low-load test before declaring it the most efficient'. powerstations.reviews gives the TRAIL 300 DC only as EcoFlow's 0.01 W spec and says it measured nothing. outagemath says 'makers don't publish idle draw' and gives no model figures. wattpowerstation's small-loads guide has AC-on idle watts for big stations from The Solar Lab and Outdoor Life, plus one DC-only figure: DELTA Pro 3 at about 13 W (Hobotech). It has nothing for the small DC-first stations. The Technology Man's EB3A figure (16% in 12 hours with DC on) was already cited, so that one adds nothing new. Only the per-load C300X DC results and the measured TRAIL 300 DC idle are missing from every rival.
decides: This confirms the Anker SOLIX C300 DC / C300X DC as the pick for 'loses the least on USB and 12 V'. At a router-sized 24 W on its 12 V socket, techtest.org measured it losing about 4% (277.6 of 288 Wh), the low-load test ChatGPT said it was missing. That works out to about 11.5 h at 24 W, or about 13.9 h at 20 W if efficiency holds. The EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC is the runner-up for standby loss (about 2 Wh a day measured idle), but nobody has measured how much energy it delivers. Stations whose DC side needs the main board awake lose far more. The Technology Man saw the BLUETTI EB3A lose about 1.3% an hour with DC on and no load. Hobotech, as reported by wattpowerstation, measured about 13 W DC-only idle on the DELTA Pro 3, and at a 15 W router load that idle draw almost doubles the drain. For the Wi-Fi question this means a small DC-only 288 Wh unit run from 12 V lasts about as long per watt-hour as anything sold. The big stations win only on raw capacity, not on losses.

findings.label: Energy delivered, 12 V car socket at 2 A (about 24 W)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300X DC im Test: Die DC-only-Schwester der SOLIX C300 mit 140 W USB-C (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 21 May 2026)
findings.note: Full discharge into a load on the 12 V socket at 2 A; techtest.org reports 277.613 Wh. At 12 V/10 A (about 120 W) it measured 272.8 Wh (95%). Arithmetic: 277.6 Wh ÷ 24 W ≈ 11.6 h, or ≈ 13.9 h at 20 W if the efficiency holds. techtest.org tested the EU-named C300X DC. The US listing is 'SOLIX C300 DC'; both are 288 Wh, DC-only and have 140 W USB-C. I did not verify that the hardware is identical.
